question: A carrier air group's unit panel lists its fleet and theatre as units above it in the original: is the carrier's fleet the group's parent in the unit tree itself, or does the panel walk to the carrier's fleet? And what follows elsewhere.

addresses.name: CSingleUnitPanel::Rebuild
addresses.revises: Adds that the units above are a plain walk of higher_oob_unit_ptr with no other source - so a carrier air group's rows are its fleet and the fleet's superiors because CShip::LoadKey and CRebaseToCarrierMission::Start hang the group under the fleet, not because the panel asks the carrier.
addresses.comment: **Fills the list of a selected unit's panel.** Empties the list box `list` of the window `single_unitpanel` and adds, in order: a CParentUnitEntry for each unit above, the highest first; a CUnitView (the `unitpanel` header row); a CUnitStatusEntry; a CCurrentOrdersEntry; for a headquarters (oob_level < 4) a CObjectivesEntry, and where CUnit::HasAgentAbove the three stance entries, a CPowerRatioEntry and a CDesiredAssetsEntry; a CSingleUnitButtons; a CWindowForSubUnitsEntry; a CWindowForChildUnitsEntry where CUnit::CountChildrenShown is not 0; a CWindowForLoadedUnitsEntry for a fleet and for an air unit; a CCombatEntry for each battle. The panel's unit is at +8. **The units above are the chain of higher_oob_unit_ptr (+0x1E0) and nothing else** - built into a local list from the unit's parent upward, counted into +0x10, then walked from its end so the highest comes first; no base, carrier or ship is asked. A carrier air group shows its fleet and the fleet's superiors because it is the fleet's child in the tree (CShip::LoadKey, CRebaseToCarrierMission::Start). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitpanel.md, section 2, and FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.1 (the order of battle).
addresses.evidence: Decompiled 2026-11-14 on a scratch copy: `iVar10 = *(unit + 0x1e0); while (iVar10 != 0) { new node{iVar10, prev}; ...; iVar10 = *(iVar10 + 0x1e0); panel+0x10++ }`, then the nodes walked back through their +8 link, each becoming a CParentUnitEntry. No other read feeds the loop. Shown wrong by any other writer of the parent entries in this function, of which there is none.

addresses.name: CShip::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CShip::LoadKey(CShip* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.revises: The comment listed the one key only; adds what the `air` case does - the group is hung under the ship's fleet in the order of battle (CUnit_AttachToParent), based on the ship's carrier base, loaded and appended to the country's units; with no fleet it is read and deleted. FINDINGS-unitstart.md had this; the entry did not.
addresses.comment: **The keys its switch names**, 1 of them, one case each: `air`. Read from the switch by reversing/scripts/definitions.py. A loader may resolve further keys as names out of a database - CGovernment and CMinister both do - but anything that is neither is dropped in silence. Any other key goes to CSubUnit::LoadKey. **The `air` case** (an order of battle file's or a save's carrier group): a CAir (operator new 0x2F4) is made; where the ship has a unit (+0xB0, its fleet): CUnit vf_28 with the fleet's interface host, CUnit_SetOwner with the ship's owner, **CUnit_AttachToParent(group, fleet)** - so the group is the fleet's child in the order of battle from the moment it is read - CUnit::SetBase with the ship's embedded CUnitBaseCarrier (+0xD8), the block's Load, and CCountry::AddUnit, which appends it to the country's list. A ship with no unit reads the block and deletes the group. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.1 (the order of battle), and FINDINGS-unitstart.md.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled 2026-11-14: `if (key != air) { CSubUnit::LoadKey; return; } new CAir; if (this->unit_ptr != 0) { vf_28(unit_ptr->in_game_idler_ptr); CUnit_SetOwner(...); CUnit_AttachToParent(group, this->unit_ptr); CUnit::SetBase(group, &this->field_0xd8); Load; CCountry::AddUnit(...) } else { Load; scalar delete }`. Wrong if CUnit_AttachToParent's arguments were the other way round - its first test is the two owners and its second `parent->oob_level < child->oob_level`, fleet 5 against air 6, which only holds this way.

addresses.name: CRebaseAirOrder::IsActive
addresses.revises: Names the call the comment gave as an address only: `leaves it (0x5B9A30)` is CUnit_LeaveParent(unit, true) - the group leaves its fleet in the order of battle, for the top, not only the carrier - before CUnit::SetBase moves its base.
addresses.comment: Slot 14: false with no base. Where the unit's base is not the order's province: a unit based on a carrier (its base's slot 1, IsCarrier) is taken out of the order of battle - **CUnit_LeaveParent(unit, true)**, so a carrier group rebased to an airfield leaves its fleet for the top of the order of battle, not back to any commander it had - and CUnit::SetBase(the province's air base object, +0x54). **Where the unit is in the province every wing's organisation (CSubUnit +0x60) is halved** - org * 1000 / 2000, not under 0 - and the order is done. Otherwise, from the start hour on, FindPath; done where the unit then has no path and is in no battle. A group under a fleet whose carrier has sunk is no longer based on a carrier and stays under the fleet. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaair.md, section 3, and FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.1 (the order of battle).
addresses.evidence: Decompiled 2026-11-14: `if (home_base != 0 && (*(*home_base + 4))() != 0) CUnit_LeaveParent(unit, true); CUnit::SetBase(unit, *(province + 0x54));`. The base's slot 1 answers true only for CUnitBaseCarrier (FINDINGS-outliner.md A.4). Shown wrong if 0x5B9A30 were not CUnit_LeaveParent - its record and its decompile (unlink from higher_oob_unit_ptr's Children, parent set to null) say it is.

addresses.name: CGameState::RemoveUnit
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CGameState::RemoveUnit(CGameState* this, CUnit* unit, bool keepOfficers, bool withPassengers)
addresses.revises: Adds what becomes of the units under the removed one: each is taken out of the order of battle with CUnit_LeaveParent(child, true) and left with nobody above it - not handed to the removed unit's own superior - and a removed theatre's (oob_level 0) are marked orphaned (+0x50). So a fleet merged away leaves its carriers' groups, whose ships went to the other fleet, aboard with nobody above them.
addresses.comment:
**A unit ceases to exist**, and this is where it is destroyed.

It unlinks the unit from everything holding it - its country's units, its province, its parent's Children in the order of battle, plans and orders, the interface's selection - takes its regiments off it through RemoveRegimentFromUnit, and then calls **the unit's own scalar deleting destructor**, `unit->vftable->vf_0(1)`. So the object is freed, not handed on.

**The units under it** (+0x1E4): after CUnit::LeaveAllCombats and CUnit_LeaveParent(unit, true), each child in turn is CUnit_LeaveParent(child, true) - left at the top of the order of battle, **not handed to the removed unit's superior** - and where the removed unit is a theatre (oob_level 0) the child's `orphaned` (+0x50) is set. A fleet's children are its carriers' air groups, so a fleet merged into another (CMergeCommand::Execute: CUnit_MergeInto, then this) leaves the groups aboard the ships that went over with nobody above them.

Its callers are every place a unit is gone for good: a country capitulating or being annexed with units it cannot transfer, CDisbandCommand::Execute, and CUnit::RetreatFromCombat finding nowhere to retreat to.

**The two flags.** With the first clear, the owner's officers fall by the unit's officers times its strength share times the officer ratio, floored at nought. The second decides what becomes of what the unit carries: **a fleet's land units and an air unit's land units alike** are removed with it (RemoveUnit called on each with the same flags) where it is set, and otherwise let go where they stand - a fleet's passengers with +0x300, +0x1C8, +0x2E4 and +0x2E8 cleared, an air unit's with +0x304 and +0x2E8 - with no supplies moved and no battle looked for. The hourly removal drain, a capitulation and an annexation, and a disbanded rebel army pass it set (each recorded at its call); the government-in-exile clean-up passes it clear for a unit it destroys outright; CCountry_Reset's call was not read. So **a transport plane destroyed takes its paratroopers with it**. A land unit removed is taken off its fleet's or its plane's list. A fleet removed also lets go each carrier's air groups - out of the fleet in the order of battle, off the ship's list, a fresh null order, CAir::CheckBase and CUnit::EnterProvince where they stand - before each ship goes to DisposeSubUnit. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, sections A.5, D.1 and D.3, and FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.1 (the order of battle).
addresses.evidence: Decompiled 2026-11-14: `CUnit::LeaveAllCombats(unit); CUnit_LeaveParent(unit, true); for (node = unit->Children.first; node; ) { child = node->data; node = node->next; CUnit_LeaveParent(child, true); if (unit->oob_level == 0) child->orphaned = true; }`, then the naval branch's walk of each regiment's carried list. Agrees with the `orphaned` field's own record (VA 0x68500E). Shown wrong by any AttachToParent call on a child in this function; there is none.

addresses.name: CGameState::DisposeSubUnit
addresses.revises: Read whole on a decompile, so confirmed where it was inferred; adds that the air groups it lets go are **not** taken out of the fleet in the order of battle - no CUnit_LeaveParent - so a sunk carrier's groups stay the fleet's children (FINDINGS-transport.md D.6 said so; the entry did not).
addresses.comment: What is done with a ship, wing or brigade that is taken out of its unit for good. A ship (slot 10) whose byte +0xF4 is set (CShip's constructor sets it) has, **for each air group based on it** (CShip +0xDC): the group taken off the ship's list, its base (+0x98) cleared, a fresh null order put in (its slot 13 called), CAir::CheckBase (the nearest of its country's air bases in a straight line) and CUnit::EnterProvince where it is - **and nothing takes it out of the order of battle**, so a sunk carrier's groups stay under its fleet; and the ship is put on the game state's list at +0x20 rather than freed. Anything else is deleted at once. Called by CUnit::RemoveSpentSubUnits (a ship sunk) and by CGameState::RemoveUnit (a whole unit removed), among six. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.1, and FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.1 (the order of battle).
addresses.evidence: Decompiled 2026-11-14 whole: the IsNaval and +0xF4 test, the walk of the list at the ship's +0xDC (the decompile's subunit[1].field_0x4), each group unlinked from its base's list, home_base_ptr = 0, two CreateOrder(0x18D) with the old order destroyed, Start, CheckBase, EnterProvince, then the ship appended to sunk_ships. No call to CUnit_LeaveParent or any write of +0x1E0. Shown wrong by a write of a group's higher_oob_unit_ptr reached from here.

slots_noted: CShip slot 4 (LoadKey) and CRebaseAirOrder slot 14 (IsActive) are already recorded under these names; the entries revise comments only.
